failure_breakdown.relationship_to_R338: R338 reported 21.2% failure (overdrainage-only, P(flow>=0.5)). R339 reports 21.1% overdrainage (matches R338) PLUS 11.4% underdrainage (newly tracked). Total failure envelope = 32.5%.
failure_breakdown.interpretation: Underdrainage is a distinct failure mode that R338 did not separately track. Adding it does not change R338's overdrainage number — it adds a new dimension of failure that the CEO's audit specifically requested be made first-class.

failure_driver_analysis.finding: Underdrainage failures cluster at high P_upright (>32 mmHg) AND low P_max (<38 mmHg). Damper fully compresses before reaching patient's postural pressure, zeroing flow.

decision_boundary_table.design_intervention: None — patient variability, design around it.
Tighter manufacturing tolerance on G_max (±12% → ±6%) via precision molding.
Exponent is set by damper geometry. Redesign from n=2 (quadratic) to n=1.5 (gentler) would reduce extreme-pressure underdrainage.
None — patient variability, design around it.
Tolerance on maximum compression stop (±12% → ±6%) via mechanical hard stop.
Tolerance on threshold spring preload (±20% → ±10%) via calibration step.

repair_hypothesis.intervention: Increase P_max from 40 mmHg to 50 mmHg AND tighten P_max tolerance from ±12% to ±3%.
repair_hypothesis.tradeoff_observed: Increasing P_max reduces underdrainage (11.4% → 0.0%) but increases overdrainage (21.1% → 61.4%). This is the fundamental damper-design trade-off: you cannot simultaneously prevent both failure modes by tuning P_max alone.
repair_hypothesis.verdict: REPAIR HYPOTHESIS FAILS — increasing P_max alone trades underdrainage for overdrainage. Overdrainage: 21.1% → 61.4% (+40.3 pp). Underdrainage: 11.4% → 0.0% (-11.4 pp). Net pass rate (both criteria): 67.5% → 38.6% (-29.0 pp). More sophisticated repair needed (e.g., increase P_max AND lower G_max, or change exponent n, or different mechanism entirely). Record as MECHANISM LIMITATION until a working repair is found.
repair_hypothesis.caveat: Repair changes the operating envelope. Even if it improved pass rate, must verify the device still fits anatomical constraints (max pressure head, etc.) and does not introduce new failure modes.
alternative_repairs_to_explore: Increase P_max AND lower G_max (preserve overdrainage protection while reducing underdrainage)
Change exponent n from 2 (quadratic) to 1.5 (gentler compression curve)
Add a serial fixed orifice to cap maximum flow regardless of damper state
Two-stage damper: soft compression at low pressures, hard stop at high pressures
Accept the trade-off and constrain patient indication (exclude patients with P_upright > 35 mmHg)

knowledge_atom_proposed.if: damper pressure regime approaches extreme P_max (high P_upright + low P_max tolerance)
knowledge_atom_proposed.then: evaluate underdrainage before claiming safety margin
knowledge_atom_proposed.action: Future hydraulic inventions must declare their P_max headroom relative to expected patient P_upright distribution.
